abstract: Extreme precipitation on the central Tibetan Plateau, particularly outside the summer monsoon season, strongly affects glacier mass balance and downstream water availability, yet the moisture transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. This study combines high-resolution measurements of the isotopic composition of atmospheric water vapour at Nam Co Lake with isotope-enabled climate model simulations to investigate an extreme snowfall event on 25 October 2022. We show that the event was triggered by a cyclonic disturbance over the northern Bay of Bengal, reinforced by the western Pacific subtropical high, which channelled moisture into the plateau interior. We identify a growing class of similar cyclone-driven extreme precipitation events before and after the monsoon season from 1990 to 2022. Climate projections indicate that such events will become more frequent under moderate and high emissions. These findings identify a robust isotopic fingerprint of cyclone–orography interactions and highlight the growing role of Bay of Bengal moisture in Tibetan Plateau water security in a warming climate.

title: In the synthetic biology era, engineered fungi could mitigate carbon dioxide emissions and enhance environmental resilience
abstract: Over the past two decades, there has been a staggering increase in greenhouse gas emissions, particularly carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) from unrestrained anthropogenic activities, leading to notable environmental shifts. Despite continuous efforts to reduce emissions, the world is not making satisfactory progress, which calls for immediate action to implement alternative strategies to enhance environmental sustainability. The Earth naturally absorbs and stores carbon through various processes, but merely keeping pace with ongoing human activities is no longer sufficient. Land plants and marine prokaryotes absorb CO 2 during photosynthesis and store carbon as biomass. Eukaryotic organisms also represent a valuable resource that can provide insights into the biological fixation and removal of atmospheric CO 2 . Expanding the capacities of Earth’s natural systems offers enormous potential for enhancing carbon sinks and promoting environmental resilience. Although extensive synthetic engineering of plant systems has been conducted to enhance their native carbon fixation pathways, research on microorganisms, especially fungi, has been limited. In this review, we specifically explore the role of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, elucidating their responses to environmental shifts and their potential for climate change mitigation. We place particular emphasis on the role of various fungal guilds in this process, highlighting those that should be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications. We then engage with previous endeavors to address primary challenges in advancing genetic tools for these understudied fungi. Lastly, we discuss how integrating synthetic biology practices into the field of soil-associated fungi can drive advances in long-term carbon storage, enhance degradation of environmental pollutants, and improve nutrient exchange and soil health, contributing to more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions. Rising carbon dioxide emissions from human activities are driving environmental change and increasing the need for strategies that strengthen natural carbon sinks and ecosystem resilience. While plants and microorganisms play important roles in carbon capture and storage, the potential of soil-associated fungi remains comparatively underexplored, particularly from a synthetic biology perspective. In this Review, we examine the roles of soil-borne fungi in carbon management, their responses to environmental change, and their potential contributions to climate change mitigation. We highlight key fungal guilds that could be prioritized for future synthetic biology applications and discuss current challenges in developing genetic tools for understudied fungi. Finally, we explore how engineering soil-associated fungi could support long-term carbon storage while providing broader environmental benefits, including pollutant degradation, nutrient exchange, and improved soil health. Together, these opportunities position fungal synthetic biology as a promising approach for developing more resilient soil ecosystems and sustainable environmental interventions.

title: Emulating absent land processes reduces carbon budgets in CMIP6 models
abstract: The Transient Climate Response to cumulative Emissions (TCRE) is the cornerstone of estimates of carbon emissions budgets to future warming targets, characterising the near-linear relationship between the increase in global mean temperature and cumulative emissions of CO 2 . TCRE is derived from highly sophisticated Earth System Models (ESMs) - some, however, lack important processes known to have a large impact on TCRE. Here, we use multiple configurations of UKESM, a full-complexity ESM, to estimate how TCRE of 11 ESMs that participated in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project 6 would change if each included six terrestrial carbon cycle related processes present in UKESM, such as nitrogen limitation of photosynthesis and fire-vegetation interactions. We find that accounting for processes not included in the models increases their TCRE by an average of 21.4% implying a reduction of 16.0% ± 0.8% in the carbon budget for the transition from 1.5 °C to 2 °C.

title: Metagenomic evidence for climate-associated variation in microbial methylmercury production across peatlands
abstract: Peatlands are major global mercury (Hg) reservoirs and are highly sensitive to warming, yet climate effects on microbial controls of neurotoxic methylmercury (MeHg) formation remain unclear. Here, we combined global synthesis with new measurements to assess climate-associated variation in net MeHg production. Metagenomes from 144 peat soils revealed higher relative abundance of the Hg-methylation gene hgcA but lower relative abundance of the demethylation gene merB at high latitudes, consistent with their opposing correlations with mean annual temperature. The ratio of nitrogen-fixation to denitrification genes ( nifH / nosZ ) covaried with hgcA and merB , suggesting links between nitrogen cycling and Hg transformation. Genome-resolved analyses further showed expanded denitrification pathways in hgcA -bearing taxa from warmer peatlands. Together, these findings indicate that warmer climates may be associated with microbial community restructuring and lower net MeHg production. A space-for-time framework therefore suggests reduced MeHg yields under future warming, informing Hg-risk assessment under the Minamata Convention.

title: Inter-hemispheric contrast in the sensitivity of polar amplification to sea-ice coverage conditions
abstract: Polar amplification of near-surface warming can have substantial global implications. However, large uncertainties remain regarding its future changes and the underlying mechanisms. Here we show substantial inter-hemispheric contrast in the climate state dependence of polar amplification by analyzing both future and distant past climates. Climate model simulations indicate that both the amplitude and seasonality of Arctic amplification greatly weaken in future sea ice-free climates. A similar feature is inferred from a paleoclimate data assimilation product. Yet, pronounced cloud-related uncertainties in summer-season Arctic amplification are found in distant past climate simulations. In comparison, the intensity and seasonality of Antarctic amplification are generally weaker and also less sensitive to the climate state in both future and distant past warm climates. Although cloud-related uncertainties in summer-season Arctic amplification need to be resolved, the overall agreement between future and distant past warm climates suggests that the inter-hemispheric contrast is likely to weaken as the Arctic approaches to sea ice-free climates.

title: Differentiating Westerly and Asian monsoon dust fluxes to the tropical Pacific Ocean since the late Pliocene
abstract: Asian dust flux is a fundamental regulator of global climate and marine biogeochemical cycles, yet it is difficult to separate the dust fractions delivered to the tropical Pacific Ocean by the Westerlies and East Asian Winter Monsoon (EAWM). We present a 4-million-year record of eolian evolution from the Philippine Sea to deconvolve these two distinct transport systems on the basis of grain-size modeling and geochemical fingerprinting. Our results show that the Westerlies component is primarily derived from hyper-arid deserts, whereas the EAWM-driven component originates from the semi-arid margins of East and Central Asia. Of importance is the finding that Westerly-driven transport reflects a coherent response to global cooling and hemispheric thermal gradients, whilst the Asia monsoon contribution is mediated by vegetation cover. We further demonstrate that hydroclimatic fluctuations in EAWM marginal zones modulate dust availability through vegetation-induced surface roughness and pedogenic refinement, resulting in a pronounced non-linear relationship between dust flux and wind energetics. This suggests the ecological conditions of dust source regions exert an impact on dust flux and thus the tropical ocean, necessitating integration of dynamic vegetation impacts and anthropogenic landscape interventions on dust into Earth System Models to predict global carbon cycling in a warming world.

title: Precipitation trend uncertainty from product choice rivals or exceeds the magnitude of actual trends
abstract: Gridded precipitation products are widely used to assess long-term rainfall and snowfall change, yet their trend reliability remains uncertain. We evaluate 19 (quasi-)global products for three annual statistics: mean precipitation, daily maximum, and wet-day frequency, screening for temporal homogeneity and benchmarking trends against daily and monthly rain-gauge observations. Most products exhibit spatially coherent discontinuities linked to observing-system changes, particularly satellite-instrument transitions in the late 1990s to early 2000s and 2014–2015. Notably, only 58–64% of non-gauge-corrected products match the reference trend sign on average. Even including gauge-corrected products, the interquartile range of product trends is 1.1–1.9 times the reference magnitude, so product choice rivals or exceeds the magnitude of the trends themselves. For 1983–2025 annual-mean trends over land, the eight long-record products span and extend beyond the climate model ensemble envelope, implying observations cannot cleanly disentangle model error from observational uncertainty. This uncertainty propagates into infrastructure design, agricultural risk management, and climate finance, particularly in the tropics and Global South.

title: Black carbon aerosols intensified India’s 2015 mega heatwave and expanded heat stress exposure
abstract: Large-scale climatic drivers are known to amplify heatwave temperatures, whereas aerosols have complex regional temperature responses depending upon aerosol composition. With the help of recent observations and chemistry-coupled regional climate model simulations, we show that coincident aerosols—black carbon in particular—elevated the heatwave intensity of India’s deadly 2015 heatwave event. During the heatwave period in 2015, aerosols increased daily temperature maxima by 0.2–1.5 °C, which was spatially averaged over the heatwave-affected region. Further, increased surface humidity from aerosol-induced dynamic changes in moisture transport activated a moist heat stress episode, increasing daily wet-bulb temperature maxima by 0.25–1.8 °C. Overall, the aerosol effects additionally exposed about 30 million persons and 0.2 million km² of land area to extremely dry and moist heat stress. This highlights the need for a coordinated clean air and climate strategy, addressing the emission sources of black carbon for efficient air quality and heat stress management.

title: Amazonian rainforest bioaerosol influenced by African dust intrusion
abstract: Biological particles are an important but poorly understood component of Amazonian aerosols, having impacts on ecosystems, climate and human health. Here, we show that African dust plumes transport microbial communities across the Atlantic into the Amazon rainforest. We characterize the bacterial, fungal, and archaeal communities at 42 and 323 m above ground at the Amazon Tall Tower Observatory, both during background conditions and a five-day North African dust intrusion. Under background conditions, bacterial communities vary with height and time, reflecting diverse local and transported sources, whereas fungal communities remain stable and are dominated by locally produced fungi. During the dust intrusion, bacterial communities shift strongly towards microorganisms associated with dryland soils, biological soil crusts, and marine environments, while fungal communities remain unchanged. Additionally, airborne endotoxin concentrations increase threefold, without enriching obligate pathogens. Our findings demonstrate that African dust is not only a mineral nutrient source but also a vector of intercontinental microbial transport, with potential consequences for ecosystem functioning, atmospheric processes and human health.

title: Phototroph-specific nitrogen isotopes detail N2-fixation increases at the end-Triassic extinction
abstract: The end-Triassic mass extinction (~201.6 Ma) marked fundamental ecological and environmental disruptions triggered by the emplacement of the Central Atlantic Magmatic Province. One critically overlooked aspect of this event is the nitrogen cycle, despite its central role in regulating the carbon cycle and supporting marine ecosystems. To investigate these changes, we analyzed compound-specific nitrogen and carbon isotopes of sedimentary metalloporphyrins derived from phototrophs at a key coastal ETE locality: St. Audrie’s Bay, UK. Our porphyrin analysis provides robust constraints on the isotopic compositions of major groups of phototrophs throughout the photic zone, specifically purple and green sulfur bacteria inhabiting in and below the chemocline, along with algae and/or cyanobacteria in the overlying oxygenated surface waters. These primary producer-specific nitrogen isotopes indicate a substantial reorganization of the coastal nitrogen cycle following the end-Triassic mass extinction. In the immediate extinction aftermath, N 2 -fixation contributed up to ~90% of primary production and averaged between ~50% and ~65%. These values are substantially higher than previously reported for anoxic coastal environments, which best represent the depositional conditions at St. Audrie’s Bay. This pronounced shift toward N 2 -fixation suggests strongly stratified marine systems subjected to rapid CO 2 -forcing undergo fundamental nitrogen cycling restructuring, with important implications for future climate scenarios.

title: Wind–solar generation and scarcity resilience are spatially decoupled in Europe
abstract: The rapid expansion of wind and solar power is increasing the exposure of European electricity systems to weather-driven variability. Renewable resource assessments commonly emphasise locations with high mean resource availability, implicitly assuming that high mean generation also implies high generation during scarcity conditions. Here we show that this assumption does not hold for continent-wide wind–solar scarcity. Using daily wind and solar capacity factors for 128,931 existing European onshore wind turbine locations during 1986–2025, we identify coherent generation regimes and quantify their performance during low-generation periods. We find a clear spatial decoupling between mean generation and scarcity resilience efficiency: clusters with the highest mean generation are not necessarily those that maintain generation during scarcity, while several clusters with moderate mean generation exhibit comparatively high resilience. These results demonstrate that mean generation and scarcity resilience represent distinct spatial characteristics and provide a resource-side climatological diagnostic for assessing European wind–solar generation under continent-wide scarcity conditions.

title: Pathways to pyrite through polysulfides and metastable iron sulfides in marine sediments
abstract: The formation of pyrite (FeS₂) is a critical process in sedimentary environments, central to the global iron and sulfur cycles and sedimentary redox cycling. However, the mechanisms governing pyrite formation under natural conditions remain poorly constrained. Using Mössbauer spectroscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), we present direct evidence of polysulfides facilitating the transformation of FeS x phases into pyrite in natural sediments from Saanich Inlet, British Columbia. We identify two nanoparticulate FeS 1+x phases: a mackinawite-like phase (np-FeS 1+x −1) and a greigite-like phase (np-FeS 1+x −2). Under persistently sulfidic conditions, the greigite-like phase can compete with pyrite as the prevailing Fe-S mineral. We also demonstrate that sequential chemical extractions underestimate highly reactive nanoparticulate Fe phases owing, in part, to pyrite framboids encapsulated within diatom frustules. Notably, these findings provide direct spectroscopic evidence consistent with polysulfide-mediated Fe-S transformations in low-temperature natural sediments, bridging a long-standing gap between experimental models and environmental observations and refining our understanding of early diagenetic pyrite formation.

title: Two large unstable slopes in West Greenland illustrates an emerging Arctic tsunami hazard
abstract: Landslides entering fjords or lakes can generate tsunamis that threaten communities far beyond the source area. Here we document the active deformation of two newly identified unstable slopes within the Uummannaq Fjord system in central West Greenland: a large slope in Karrat Fjord ( ~ 400 million m³) and a smaller yet more imminent, slope in Kangerluarsuk Fjord ( ~ 30 million m³). Both were discovered following the catastrophic 2017 Karrat landslide and tsunami, which prompted closer investigations of the region. Numerical tsunami simulations indicate that a potential collapse of the Karrat unstable slope would produce a tsunami affecting the entire fjord system. The scale, location, and evolving nature of these slopes highlight the vulnerability of remote Arctic regions to landslide-induced tsunamis. Likely driven by permafrost degradation, these slopes represent an emerging hazard expected to worsen with continued Arctic warming. Our findings underscore the importance of the monitoring and risk mitigation efforts by local authorities in these rapidly changing high-latitude environments.

title: A process-based screening framework for coastal reservoirs
abstract: Reservoirs underpin global water supply, yet new upland storage is increasingly constrained by topography, ecosystems, and social acceptance. Coastal reservoirs, impounding river discharge in estuaries and lagoons, offer an alternative, but early-stage suitability is shaped by coupled risks from salinity, marine forcing, water quality, and shoreline change. We develop a transferable, process-based screening framework of five screening dimensions and 16 ordinal indicators, with numerical modules (salinity transport, sea-state transformation, morphodynamics) placing all candidate sites on a consistent present-day basis for quantitative comparison. Applied to three coastal archetypes in southern Taiwan, suitability depends on coupled controls rather than hydrology alone: reservoir geometries influence freshening, and offshore wave statistics poorly proxy nearshore loads. Rankings are robust to weighting, and diagnosed weaknesses can be improved by design refinement and re-screening. The framework enables transparent, reproducible cross-site comparison and provides actionable screening criteria to support climate-informed, resilient coastal water-storage planning.

title: Slow craton thickening can increase the frequency of kimberlite eruptions
abstract: Although cratons are stabilized by their thick and highly viscous lithosphere, their long-term thermal evolution remains poorly understood. Here, kimberlite-hosted mantle xenoliths can provide constraints on past craton thickness, as they erupt almost exclusively beneath thick cratons that protrude into a ‘kimberlite window’ of 160–250 km. Global compilations indicate that kimberlite eruptions become more frequent and continuous after 1500 Ma. Therefore, we link two fundamental questions: how craton thickness evolved through time, and whether this evolution influenced kimberlite magmatism. We present 27 two-dimensional numerical models of craton evolution within a convecting mantle, and explore the effects of initial craton thickness, compositional buoyancy, radiogenic heating, and mantle cooling. Although cratons originated as hot and thick layers in the Archean, gravitational flattening likely thinned them above kimberlite-generating depths. With progressive cooling, craton viscosity and density increased, allowing cratons to undergo gradual thickening after ~ 2000 Ma. We conclude that thickening processes, such as tectonic compression and cooling, operate faster than thinning processes, such as sub-lithospheric dripping, to slowly thicken cratons into the ‘kimberlite window’. Such thickening is a possible explanation for the increasing frequency of kimberlite eruptions after ~ 1500 Ma.

title: The finance sector should capture the full range of climate change risks
abstract: Climate risk assessments used by the financial sector are often based on empirical data from recent decades that do not span the full range of possible futures. We argue that the financial sector needs to embrace risk analysis for all plausible scenarios, not just for median outcomes.

title: Unprecedented storm impact in the Mediterranean revealed by models and seismic noise during Cyclone Harry
abstract: Between 19 and 22 January 2026, the extratropical Cyclone Harry generated the highest individual wave height ever recorded in the Mediterranean Sea, causing widespread coastal flooding and erosion across the central basin. Here we combine oceanographic and meteorological observations, high-resolution morphodynamic datasets, hydrodynamic modelling, and regional microseism analysis to show that Harry produced the most severe coastal impacts of any Mediterranean cyclone in recent decades. Process-based XBeach and HEC-RAS simulations across 19 coastal sites in Sardinia, Malta, Sicily, and Calabria reveal unprecedented inundation extents strongly modulated by local geomorphology, with submarine canyons, buried palaeo-channels, and urban infrastructure amplifying wave setup and inland flooding. Concurrently, broadband seismic records from 55 Mediterranean stations show exceptional secondary microseism amplification, with Ionian stations reaching the highest amplitudes since the beginning of seismic recordings in 1990. Harry’s Microseism Reduced Amplitude exceeded previous storms and Mediterranean cyclones by more than fourfold, highlighting escalating coastal risk under climate-driven cyclone intensification.

title: Global warming intensifies compound renewable energy droughts
abstract: The transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy is essential for mitigating human-induced climate change and achieving climate neutrality, requiring reliable and resilient renewable energy systems. However, global warming is expected to increase the instability of renewable energy resources, particularly during periods of simultaneous low wind and solar power generation, known as renewable energy droughts. Here, we investigate renewable energy droughts globally under 1.5 ∘ , 2 ∘ and 3 ∘ C global warming levels using CMIP6 multi-model simulations, explicitly capturing their compound nature and the joint dependence between wind and solar resources. Results show that renewable energy droughts intensify progressively with warming, with statistically significant changes in duration, frequency, and intensity affecting 69.4%, 74.0%, and 50.2% of the global land area, respectively, at 3 ∘ C global warming level. Machine learning analysis identifies solar radiation as the dominant driver of renewable energy drought intensification, with influence strengthening under higher global warming levels. These findings highlight the need to integrate compound risk assessments into renewable energy planning to ensure system reliability in a warming world.

title: Persistent influx of atmospheric microplastics and nanoplastics to Mount Everest driven by large scale circulation
abstract: The Third Pole receives long-range transported pollutants, yet atmospheric micro- and nanoplastics inputs remain poorly constrained. Here we report year-long monitoring on the northern slope of Mount Everest using dry, wet, and total deposition sampling. Microplastic deposition fluxes at Qomolangma Station (64.0 n m −2 d −1 ) significantly exceed those at Everest Base Camp (23.0 n m −2 d −1 ), reflecting topographic and anthropogenic differences. Deposited microplastics are dominated by fragments, mainly polyamide, polyethylene terephthalate, and polyethylene. Nanoplastic concentrations across five representative months are higher at Qomolangma Station than at Everest Base Camp and include polyethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polyvinyl chloride, and polypropylene. Monsoon periods enhance wet deposition via short-range transport, whereas non-monsoon periods receive long-range continental inputs. Upscaling suggests an annual atmospheric input of 56.4 tons of microplastic to the Tibetan Plateau above 4000 m. These results identify the atmosphere as an efficient pathway for plastic delivery to the Third Pole, with potential ecological risks despite low ambient concentrations.

title: Global warming and the Pacific Decadal Oscillation drive seasonally varying increases in extreme fire weather over the southwestern US
abstract: Wildfire activity has increased across the western United States (US), with evidence linking these trends to anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we analyze the frequency, intensity, and drivers of fire weather extremes in the southwestern US over the past 83 years. These extremes exhibit strong seasonality: wintertime changes align with long-term warming trends, while summertime variations are dominated by decadal fluctuations modulated by the Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO). Fire risk has increased steadily during December–May, outside the traditional fire season, primarily due to rising temperatures and declining relative humidity (RH). In contrast, summertime fire risk, largely governed by humidity, follows a roughly V-shaped trajectory, decreasing from 1940-1980 and then rising from 1981-2022, in close alignment with decadal shifts in the PDO. Although Earth system models reliably capture temperature-related changes, they underestimate interdecadal variability in humidity, manifested by a weak representation of the observed PDO–RH relationship and low-RH extremes in summer.

title: Diversified cropping rotation increases soil carbon sequestration via fungal-mediated necromass production and mineral association
abstract: Crop diversification boosts soil organic carbon (SOC) storage, yet uncertainty persists regarding its effects on molecular SOC composition. Using a 43-year field trial in fluvo-aquic soil, we contrasted conventional wheat-rice (ConCrop) versus diversified rice/wheat – cotton/barley – maize/faba bean rotations (DivCrop). We demonstrated DivCrop elevated SOC by 9.6% (0–15 cm) and 15% (15–30 cm). DivCrop alleviated C-nitrogen co-limitation, stimulating 150% greater microbial growth and 47% higher C use efficiency. This coincided with restructured microbial communities shifting toward fungal dominance and increased functional capacity. Community transplantation assays confirmed increased adaptation for efficient C processing. Diversification accelerated lignin decomposition (plant-derived C reduced by 19–35%) and redirecting C flow toward fungal necromass (20–44% of total microbial necromass). Consequently, mineral-associated organic C increased 48–69%, with short-term formation efficiency rising 98–160% via reactive iron oxide interactions. Diversification thus shifts plant-derived recalcitrance towards mineral-stabilized microbial products in low-SOC soils, reshaping SOC composition toward climate-resilient agriculture.

title: Non-analog environments supported early Homo sapiens in southern Africa 200 000 years ago
abstract: In our species’ evolutionary history, the type of environments in which we evolved can provide crucial details about early human adaptive capacities. Such environments might not exist under current climatic and ecological conditions. Reconstructing palaeohydrology and vegetation using multiple proxies at human fossil sites in South Africa provides insights into local conditions at a high level of detail. This paper presents a plant n -alkane stable isotope record for Florisbad and Lombard’s Drift, which is anchored by new luminescence ages that revise the age for the Florisbad human cranium. We observe contrasting, non-analog plant environments during the Middle and Late Pleistocene by combining multiple lines of evidence to better understand the different environments that early Homo sapiens experienced. It also provides the foundation to evaluate their cultural adaptation strategies through time.

title: Integrating local and landscape management promotes biodiversity, multifunctionality and yields in tropical agroforests
abstract: Reconciling food production and biodiversity conservation requires socio-ecologically viable agroecosystems. To meet this goal, tropical agroforestry must balance yield-biodiversity trade-offs through local and landscape-level management. By integrating assessments of multi-taxa diversity, biocontrol, pollination, crop pests, soil fertility, microclimate, and yield in Amazonian cacao agroforests, we identified ecological-economic synergies. Yield gains were not associated with species loss. Instead, agroforests with high spatial and vertical shade-tree heterogeneity embedded in landscapes combining 30–35% forest cover and 40–45% of other arboreal habitats (e.g., orchards/agroforests) achieved the highest biodiversity and yields. In these landscapes, flying-vertebrate-mediated arthropod suppression doubled cacao yields. Increasing agroforest shade-tree cover from ≈15% to ≈80% yielded a four-fold rise in cacao fruit-set, tripled soil potassium and enhanced thermal buffering. But light limitation, rather than pest pressure, reduced harvestable yields above 30% shade-tree cover. Our findings demonstrate that combined agroforest-level and landscape-scale management can align biodiversity conservation and economic returns in tropical landscapes.

title: Large intraplate earthquakes on an extinct oceanic plate reveal fracture zone reactivation
abstract: Oceanic fracture zones, the inactive traces of former transform faults, are often considered tectonically inactive once relative plate motion across them ceases. However, their long-term mechanical behavior and role in intraplate deformation remain poorly understood. Here, we analyze two earthquakes of Mw 7.5 and Mw 7.6 that occurred about 15 km and 49 days apart in 2025 within the Phoenix Plate, along a structure spatially consistent with a former oceanic transform fault in the Drake Passage region. These events indicate that such structures remain lithosphere-scale zones of mechanical weakness and can be reactivated under present-day stress conditions. We propose here that inherited fault geometry and regional far-field stresses associated with Scotia–Antarctic plate interactions collectively promote strain localization on these presumed fossil structures. Our results indicate that the cessation of plate-boundary activity does not imply mechanical quiescence, and that oceanic fracture zones represent long-lived zones of intraplate weakness that can both host large-magnitude earthquakes and facilitatevolcanic emplacement, as shown by a seismic reflection profile crossing the fracture zone near the earthquake epicenters. This structure acts as a lithosphere-scale tear fault within the slow subducting Phoenix slab beneath the South Shetland continental block. This behavior has implications for the mechanical evolution of oceanic lithosphere and for the interpretation of intraplate seismicity near extinct plate boundaries.

title: Erosion carbon dynamics extend beyond carbon accounting to ecological significance
abstract: For decades, the debate over whether erosion acts as a carbon source or sink has advanced our understanding of carbon redistribution across stocks and fluxes. Yet, this quantitative perspective alone does not capture the full ecological significance of carbon along these pathways. Carbon value lies not only in how much is stored, but also in how it functions within ecosystems. Erosion is not merely a switch governing land–atmosphere carbon exchange, but also a driver redistributing carbon among ecological states. Here, a framework is developed that interprets erosion as a reorganization of the soil functional layer, linking carbon redistribution to changes in stability and functionality across landscape contexts. This perspective helps explain the paradox in erosion management, whereby processes that reduce carbon burial may simultaneously enhance ecosystem functioning. It reframes carbon redistribution from changes in carbon stocks to shifts in ecological states, with implications for carbon accounting and ecosystem management.

title: Widespread tree-cover gains across Europe over two decades were strongest in regions of agricultural retreat
abstract: Changes in canopy cover and spatial arrangement of trees can strongly influence ecosystem functioning and biodiversity. Yet, long-term, continent-wide assessments have largely focused on tree cover alone. Here, we develop an integrated framework quantifying tree cover, connectivity, and tree-cover heterogeneity, and assess their dynamics across Europe from 2001 to 2021. We further examine how trends in these metrics are associated with forest management regimes, agricultural retreat, natural disturbances, climate and human activities. The most widespread combination of structural trends, covering 23% of the analyzed area, combined increasing tree cover and connectivity with declining heterogeneity. At the landscape scale, 0.25° grid cells with larger fractions of former cropland tended to exhibit more positive trends in tree cover and connectivity and more negative trends in heterogeneity. These contrasting trajectories show that tree-cover gains do not necessarily coincide with increasing tree-cover heterogeneity, with potential benefits for carbon accumulation and forest-associated species but possible costs for species dependent on open or structurally heterogeneous habitats.

title: Distinct intraseasonal pathways driving rapidly escalating heat extremes in North China and their subseasonal predictability
abstract: Rapidly escalating heat extremes, characterized by abrupt onset and limited preparation time, pose disproportionate risks to public health, agriculture, and regional economies, yet their governing mechanisms and subseasonal predictability remain poorly understood. Here we identify 107 such events over North China during the summers of 1940–2024 and classify them into four spatial types. Thermodynamic and circulation analyses show that rapid warming arises from different combinations of horizontal warm advection and subsidence-induced adiabatic heating. The four types are linked to distinct intraseasonal circulation patterns involving tropical convection, mid–high-latitude wave trains, or their interference. Forecasts from subseasonal-to-seasonal dynamical prediction systems show a consistent hierarchy: events driven mainly by tropical intraseasonal variability are the most predictable, whereas events associated with two extratropical wave trains have the lowest skill. These results establish a process-based framework linking intraseasonal dynamics to rapid heat escalation and provide a physical basis for improving subseasonal prediction of high-impact heat extremes.

title: Polar front jet regulates tropical sea surface temperature impacts on South China extreme precipitation
abstract: Extreme precipitation over South China is commonly attributed to tropical sea surface temperature forcing, yet the role of extratropical circulation remains unclear. Using observational and reanalysis data, Rossby wave propagation diagnostics and numerical experiments, we investigate record-breaking April–May 2024 rainfall. Here we show that a trough between anomalous anticyclones over the tropical western North Pacific and Northeast Asia drives moisture convergence over South China. The tropical anticyclone enhanced moisture transport into South China, whereas the Northeast Asian anticyclone suppressed moisture export, favoring moisture accumulation. While the tropical anticyclone was forced by Indian Ocean sea surface temperature anomalies, the Northeast Asian anticyclone developed within a midlatitude Rossby wave train initiated by tropical Atlantic convection and guided by a transient eddy-driven polar front jet. European Center for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts model reproduced tropical forcing but underestimated precipitation because of the polar front jet biases. These findings highlight the importance of extratropical flow for predicting tropical-forced extremes.

title: Radiation regimes shape microbial light-harvesting strategies and network organization on glacier surfaces
abstract: Glacier cryoconite hosts metabolically active microbial communities despite exposure to solar radiation, which both provides energy and imposes stress. However, how radiation regimes are associated with microbial energy acquisition strategies and ecosystem organization remains unclear. Here, we analyzed 85 cryoconite metagenomes, including 47 from Arctic glaciers and 38 from Tibetan Plateau glaciers, representing contrasting long-term radiation environments. Arctic communities show greater representation of rhodopsin-based phototrophic pathways, whereas Tibetan Plateau communities show higher potential for photosynthetic pathways. These differences are associated with distinct community structures and interaction networks. Tibetan Plateau microbiomes exhibit higher network complexity, with phototrophic taxa as highly connected network nodes, while Arctic networks are simpler and centered on rhodopsin-containing heterotrophs. Functional trait analyses further indicate higher biomass production potential in Tibetan Plateau communities. Together, our results reveal that radiation regimes are associated with divergent microbial energy acquisition strategies, with consequences for community organization and ecosystem metabolic potential in glacier cryoconite ecosystems.

title: Sedimentary controls on pyrite sulfur isotopes in euxinic settings
abstract: Pyrite is widely used to reconstruct ancient euxinic (anoxic and sulfidic) conditions, yet whether its sulfur isotope composition ( δ 34 S) preserves primary water-column signals remains debated. Here, we show combined bulk and microscale δ 34 S data from pyrite grains collected across the Black Sea water-column and deep-basin sediments. Water-column-derived pyrite consists exclusively of framboidal grains with narrow size and δ 34 S ranges, consistent with formation from local aqueous sulfide and minimal alteration during nucleation and settling. Upon sedimentation, however, these grains undergo progressive textural and isotopic modification. With increasing burial, framboids are supplemented by larger, more 34 S-enriched recrystallized grains formed during dissimilatory sulfate reduction in diffusion-limited sedimentary microenvironments. Only ≈17% of pyrite grains that match WC framboids in size, texture, and δ 34 S signature retain a water-column-consistent isotopic composition in the uppermost sediment, declining to ≤4% at depth. Sulfide profiles and gene abundances further indicate that most water-column sulfide diffuses upward from sediments. Consequently, δ 34 S records from black shales likely integrate complex diagenetic histories rather than reflect direct snapshots of WC chemistry.

title: Transitional calcite-aragonite stacking as a signature of hexagonal aragonite in biogenic and inorganic deposits
abstract: Aragonite abundantly crystallizes in marine and continental environments and occurs ubiquitously in biominerals, despite being metastable under ambient conditions. To resolve this apparent contradiction, we studied the crystal structure of aragonite that grew on calcite of biogenic (Berger Károly cave; Hungary) and inorganic (Sonnenberg; Italy and Erzberg; Austria) origin, in a range of natural settings and temperatures. Electron microscopy measurements show (001) stacking faults (SFs) in the first-grown aragonite. Structural modeling combined with theory-based optimization suggests that the crystal structure of this new type of SF can be explained by the presence of (0001) calcite-like layers within aragonite. Abundant (0001) calcite twins occur in the last-grown calcite, and hexarag, the hypothetical hexagonal polymorph of aragonite, was identified across the calcite twin interfaces. Oxygen isotope data indicate that both the Berger-Károly and Sonnenberg samples formed under non-equilibrium conditions, whereas the Erzberg aragonite formed near equilibrium, possibly explaining the defect-free structure. The presence of (001) SFs and (0001) calcite twins testifies to the formation of transitional calcite-aragonite structures, suggests the occurrence of a hexarag precursor phase, and provides new insights into the long-debated mechanism of metastable aragonite formation in dynamically evolving (bio)geologic environments.

title: Environmental flexibility across dynamic Cambrian ecosystems fueled trilobite success
abstract: Trilobites, Paleozoic arthropods, have been viewed as marine animals. Using multiproxy geochemical analyses, we suggest that Cambrian Series 2 to early Miaolingian strata in Morocco, preserving three-dimensional trilobites, record deposition within a river- and wave-influenced delta with variable salinity and episodic freshwater influence, including brackish conditions. These populations persisted through environmental transitions, spanning cool, oxic, low-salinity arid conditions with periodic freshwater input during Cambrian Stage 3-4 to warmer, more humid, increasingly saline, and anoxic settings at the transition to Wuliuan. This transition coincides with an increase in trilobite body-size and the emergence of more stable, deeper, and marine salinity environments that could have contributed to enhanced biomineralization, ecological specialization, and habitat broadening. Smaller-bodied Stage 3–4 trilobites appear adapted to dynamic shelves, whereas larger-bodied Wuliuan forms exploited increasingly stable conditions that may have favored size enlargement and exoskeletal thickening. These patterns suggest a potential link between environmental conditions and body-size distribution, with possible implications for ecological structuring across Cambrian ecosystems.

title: Algal-bacterial synergy in marimo granules enables low-carbon advanced nitrogen removal from wastewater
abstract: Marimo, a natural microalgal-bacterial consortium, represents a low-carbon solution for nitrate pollution control in low-nutrient waters. However, the adaptation of its nitrogen-cycling network to fluctuating nitrate levels remains poorly understood. This study reveals that elevated nitrate drives water matrix-dependent metabolic shifts, enhancing denitrification and assimilatory nitrate reduction performance in oligotrophic lake water, while strengthening dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium in carbon-richer wastewater treatment plant effluent. Metagenomic analysis shows that this reprogramming is coordinated by a functionally specialized core consortium, with Rhodobacteraceae as the keystone driver of nitrate reduction. Meanwhile, correlation analysis further demonstrates that nitrate functions as an environmental filter, enriching this consortium to sustain high nitrate removal efficiency, endogenous nitrogen recycling, and symbiotic stability. Overall, these findings offer insights into the microbial mechanisms underlying the stable nitrate removal performance of marimo and can guide the design of low-carbon marimo-based treatment systems under fluctuating nitrate conditions.

title: Energetically extreme fires drive disastrous societal impacts
abstract: Societally disastrous fires are often physically extreme. Using a global fire events dataset spanning 2002–2025, we demonstrate that 66% of disaster-linked fires rank in the top 0.5% globally for size, peak daily speed, or peak daily energy. Fire energy emerges as the dominant driver of these disasters, with the median energy of disaster-linked fires ranking in the 99.8th percentile of fires globally. In temperate conifer forests, primarily those in Western North America, the burned area from energetically extreme fires more than doubled during this period. The Global South accounted for 95% of total population exposure and 76% of powerline exposure to energetically extreme fires. These findings underscore the need for improved extreme fire prediction and mitigation efforts to protect lives, homes, and livelihoods.

title: Household affordability of sanitary landfilling is governed by cost allocation rather than metropolitan economic capacity
abstract: Open dumping remains a dominant municipal solid waste disposal practice globally, including in megacities whose populations and economic output rival that of small countries. Sanitary landfilling is a common transition away from open dumping, yet system-level feasibility does not translate into household affordability. Here we quantify this divergence using an integrated city-scale framework that combines spatial landfill siting, engineering-based net-present-value modeling, and satellite-derived metropolitan gross domestic product. Applying this framework across six developing megacities with over 100 million residents, we find that all cities possess surplus land meeting screening-level suitability criteria. Required cost-recovery tipping fees range from 54–130 US dollars per tonne, with 5 th –95 th -percentile intervals of ±25%–30% under joint parameter uncertainty. Under full household cost recovery, these fees imply annual disposal costs equivalent to 1.2%–2.0% of the minimum wage, whereas associated revenue requirements represent only 0.26%–1.04% of metropolitan gross domestic product. Across cities, household affordability is uncorrelated with metropolitan economic capacity. Landfill depth is the dominant engineering control on affordability, particularly in high-rainfall systems, but cost allocation exerts greater leverage than any design parameter. Thus, technically and macroscopically feasible landfills may remain difficult to sustain through direct household cost recovery without cross-subsidization and public financing.

title: Accelerating anthropogenic influence on annual peak wood density and associated carbon accumulation across northern conifers
abstract: Northern coniferous forests hold significant climatic and ecological importance, yet the optimal air temperature (OAT) governing their annual peak wood density remains unknown. Here, using tree-ring maximum latewood density (MXD) from 14,000 samples at 551 sites, we reveal an OAT range of 15–21 °C governing annual MXD variability, a more sensitive thermal metric than seasonal temperature. Reconstructions of large-scale (40°–73°N) weighted average OAT hours since 1690 show unprecedented increases over the past 30 years (~10% above the 1850–1900 baseline), driven by anthropogenic warming. Higher OAT hours are associated with an estimated average annual increase of 0.23 mg biomass (0.12 mg carbon) per 1 cm² stem surface area within the latewood increment during 1921–1994. Projections show OAT hours during 2050–2100 reaching up to 23.3% above the 1850–1900 baseline, with stronger northern increases reducing the latitudinal disparity. These results imply that assuming static density may underestimate the density-related carbon contribution in northern conifers under warming.

title: Microclimate persistence in island montane cloud forests
abstract: Montane cloud forests (MCFs), ecosystems critically dependent on persistent cloud immersion and high moisture availability, have been presumed vulnerable to regional warming and atmospheric drying. Yet their microclimatic resilience under regional climate variability remains poorly understood. Here we show that MCFs maintain remarkably stable near-surface relative humidity (RH), despite sustained regional warming, using a 42-year (1980–2021) high-resolution (2-km, hourly) climate dataset from Taiwan. These forests also exhibit substantially lower interannual RH variability than adjacent non-cloud-forested regions. This persistence arises from an interplay of mechanisms, including local and nonlocal water vapor supply under variable rainfall regimes, cloud-mediated temperature moderation, and nonlinear thermodynamic regulation. Together, these processes buffer MCFs against atmospheric drying. Our results complement prevailing assessments of MCF vulnerability to changing climate, by revealing their retention of a stable microclimate amid regional climate fluctuations. This study advances understanding of how mountain ecosystems regulate their microclimate and provides a mechanistic framework for evaluating microclimate persistence in cloud forests worldwide.

title: Self-supervised temporal reconstruction of reanalysis fields at subhourly scales
abstract: Fast-evolving weather events develop on 5–15-min timescales and can influence human activities and planning. However, most atmospheric reanalyses provide data every 1–3 h, making rapid changes difficult to capture. Traditional machine-learning approaches require high-frequency supervision labels, which limits their use when such data are unavailable. Here we present a token-guided self-supervised framework that learns temporal relationships directly from coarse archives and reconstructs subhourly fields without subhourly labels. Temporal context and the requested output time are encoded as discrete tokens and incorporated through cross-attention, enabling the model to generate intermediate states consistent with the surrounding coarse fields. Across the evaluated settings, the framework yields lower reconstruction errors than recurrent and attention-based baselines. Applied to the 1806–1900 subset of the NOAA Twentieth Century Reanalysis version 3, the framework produces 15-min ensembles of near-surface relative humidity and 2-m temperature. These reconstructions support analyses of short-term variability in historical weather records and extend event-scale analysis to periods with sparse observations.

title: Reduced, fluorine-enriched mantle preconditions giant tin mineralization
abstract: Mantle redox conditions and halogen budgets influence crustal ore formation, yet mantle domains beneath intraplate magmatic provinces remain poorly understood. Here we combine zircon oxybarometry and apatite halogen data from 1,515 zircon and 309 apatite grains in Mesozoic mafic rocks across South China to investigate the underlying mantle. We identify a previously unrecognized domain that produced reduced, fluorine-enriched mafic magmas. This domain lies distal to the Paleo-Pacific subduction front and coincides with the world-class South China tin province, contrasting with the more oxidized, less fluorine-enriched magmas of the continental-margin arc. We attribute this signature to metasomatic enrichment involving phlogopite-bearing assemblages. Such a mantle reservoir may precondition tin-fertile transcrustal magmatic systems by stabilizing divalent tin, suppressing tetravalent tin incorporation into early titanium-bearing minerals, and promoting tin enrichment in highly differentiated, fluorine-rich melts. These findings highlight the redox and halogen architecture of the mantle as a key deep-seated control on continental-scale tin metallogeny.

title: Cascading impacts of Atlantic meridional overturning circulation weakening and collapse on marine biogeochemistry
abstract: As Earth’s surface temperature continues to warm, the Atlantic meridional overturning circulation risks crossing a tipping point. Then, multiple Earth system components may be irreversibly altered. Here, we use the NASA-GISS Earth System Model to investigate the responses of ocean carbon uptake, net primary productivity, oxygen concentration, and carbon storage to a collapse of the overturning circulation under a moderate forcing scenario. We find that the sign of the impact in different systems is regionally-dependent, and the magnitude is generally larger in the Northern Hemisphere. We use a Least-Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator regression to provide estimates of the timescales over which these impacts begin to occur (lags) and are fully realized (latencies). Timescales are generally found to increase southward from the Northern high latitudes to the Southern Ocean, but are remarkably similar between different basins at similar latitudes. Tipping of the overturning circulation will lock-in committed changes to the Earth system that will take 2-3 centuries to fully unfold.
